chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who intended to recite in one chapter but began in another. He said: 'Let him return to the first chapter, unless he recites Surah Al-Ikhlas (Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad).'
I said: A man who prayed Friday prayer and intended to recite Surah Al-Jumu'ah but recited 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad'. He said: 'He returns to Surah Al-Jumu'ah.'
And from him, from Safwan, from Al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both):
Regarding a man who intends to recite Surah Al-Jumu'ah in the Friday prayer but recites 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad', he said: 'He returns to Surah Al-Jumu'ah.'

key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad (Surah Al-Ikhlas, Chapter 112)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if I start reciting a Surah in prayer but switch to Surah Al-Ikhlas?
ai.summary: This ruling from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the juristic preference for fulfilling the specific intention (niyyah) of reciting the named Surah during Friday prayers, treating Surah Al-Ikhlas as a substitute rather than a full replacement in this context. The exception for Al-Ikhlas in general prayers reflects its status as a 'third of the Quran,' yet the Friday-specific requirement underscores the ritual importance of reciting the eponymous Surah Al-Jumu'ah to complete the distinct character of the congregational prayer.
